items.name: CSF: Contextual Safety Filtering for Motion Generators
items.title: CSF: Contextual Safety Filtering for Motion Generators
items.description: Text-conditioned motion generators produce trackable whole-body motion, but they have no notion of scene-dependent safety: the same action may target an object or a person. Existing safeguards either inspect the prompt, require labeled motion data, or enforce geometric constraints; therefore, they do not directly account for how scene context changes a motion's meaning. items.title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot
items.description: METR's 50\% time horizon measures the human completion time of software tasks that an AI solves with 50\% probability, allowing AI capabilities to be expressed in interpretable units. On 228 tasks and 26 AIs, we recompute the time horizons using splines and item-response theory to relax the assumption that the AI difficulty of a task depends linearly on the log of human time. items.name: A Balanced Data Diet: Addressing the Exploration Bottleneck in Mega-Scale RL for Robot Control
items.title: A Balanced Data Diet: Addressing the Exploration Bottleneck in Mega-Scale RL for Robot Control
items.description: General-purpose robots must perform a wide range of tasks from agile locomotion to dexterous manipulation. While sim-to-real reinforcement learning (RL) has proven to be a useful tool for this goal, current RL pipelines depend on engineering-heavy, per-task structural priors such as shaped rewards and demonstrations. items.name: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
items.title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
items.description: We propose BrickBench, a benchmark for agentic text-conditioned LEGO-set design. Given a prompt, an agent is tasked with producing an assembly that not only satisfies semantic and design criteria, but that can also be physically built. To do so, it must select parts from a discrete library and reason jointly about local and global constraints. items.title: One Block, Multiple Depths: Recurrent Vision Transformers with Depth-Programmed Experts
items.description: In this work, we show that a single Transformer block, applied recurrently, can match the accuracy of a full-depth vision encoder at comparable inference FLOPs without intermediate feature distillation. reViT restores depth-specific transformations by representing the FFN at each recurrent depth as a convex combination of a small shared expert bank. items.name: Bi-FORK: Generative Modeling of High-Dimensional Bifurcating Systems
items.title: Bi-FORK: Generative Modeling of High-Dimensional Bifurcating Systems
items.description: Bifurcations are ubiquitous in physical systems, from structural buckling to fluid and climate dynamics, yet they remain largely unexplored in deep learning. At a symmetry-breaking bifurcation, a single input admits multiple equally valid solutions, violating the one-to-one assumption underlying most learned physical surrogates. items.name: Caught in the Act: Probes Effectively Detect Sabotage and Catch Unverbalized Deception
items.title: Caught in the Act: Probes Effectively Detect Sabotage and Catch Unverbalized Deception
items.description: Recent incidents have highlighted the challenge of monitoring LLM agents and the danger of models deceiving people. We show that white-box deception detection via probes can be scaled up to frontier monitoring settings by collecting the largest deception dataset to date for training probes and introducing a novel probe architecture which can aggregate information across many layers and tokens. items.title: VioLA: Learning Generalist Humanoid Control Policies from Human Data
items.description: Teaching a humanoid to follow instructions with its whole body runs into two obstacles. Its action space is large and tightly coupled: legs, arms, and fingers must move together while the robot keeps its balance, which makes joint-level actions hard to learn. items.title: FAITH: Feasibility-Aware Safety-Filtered RL for High-Dimensional Systems
items.description: Safe reinforcement learning commonly places safety and task performance in the same policy objective, where they can introduce competing updates. Safety filters separate them at action execution, but classical designs require an analytic safety function and dynamics model, and standard minimal-intervention filters are myopic to long-horizon task return because they minimize only instantaneous action deviation. items.title: Toward Joint Optimization of Circuit Depth and Training Data Size in Adaptively Grown Quantum Classifiers
items.description: Building a quantum model involves a tradeoff: how complex the circuit should be, and how much training data it needs. Caro et al. show that models with fewer trainable gates need less training data to generalize well. Q-FLAIR shows that a quantum feature-map circuit can be grown gate-by-gate, stopping once further growth stops improving the training loss. items.title: FastBench: Can Streaming VLMs Perceive High-Dynamic Real-World Streams?
items.description: Streaming Video Large Language Models (VLMs) enable continuous video understanding, yet existing benchmarks focus on low-dynamic scenarios. items.title: RoboRSI: Stable, efficient, and reusable robot self-evolution in complex real-world environments
items.description: A generalist robot should not only perform diverse tasks but also improve through experience, turning what it learns during execution into capabilities that later tasks can reuse. items.title: Beyond Spatio-Temporal Priors: A Generalizable Approach for Dense Correspondence Matching
items.description: Dense correspondence matching has historically been bounded by simplifying spatio-temporal priors, such as smooth motion and rigid geometry. items.name: A Unified Bellman Operator for Safety-Critical Reinforcement Learning
items.title: A Unified Bellman Operator for Safety-Critical Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Reinforcement learning in safety-critical domains requires maximizing task performance while strictly adhering to safety constraints. Existing safe reinforcement learning paradigms typically force a trade-off: they either require a priori knowledge to provide strict safety guarantees (e.g., safety filters), or they enable joint learning but only satisfy safety constraints on average. items.title: WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs
items.description: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) struggle with spatial, embodied, physical, and temporal reasoning. items.title: MAMHOI: Factorizing Scene-Aware Human-Object Interaction through Affordances
items.description: Generating realistic human-object interactions (HOI) in complex 3D scenes requires two complementary capabilities: reasoning about interaction feasibility in the environment and synthesizing realistic human-object motion. items.title: Predicting Alignment Generalization with Value Representations
items.description: LLM developers post-train their models to exhibit prosocial values and behavioral traits, which are enumerated in an alignment target. items.description: Safety benchmarks typically report one overall score for a suite of datasets, each of which may target one or more safety-related attributes, so models with similar overall scores can have very different attribute profiles. items.title: ViSkill: Reinforcing VLM Agents with Evolving Visual-Native Skills
items.description: Skill-augmented agents improve sample efficiency by distilling successful trajectories into reusable strategies. items.title: SpaceCast-Bench: Evaluating Predictive Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
items.description: Existing spatial reasoning benchmarks mainly test spatial perception: reading off relations already visible in the input. items.title: Learning Kilometer-Scale Weather Prediction with Global-Regional Alignment
items.description: Kilometer-scale regional weather forecasting is essential for local weather warnings and weather-sensitive decisions. items.title: SpaceFlow: Locally Controllable 3D Generation
items.description: Current 3D generation methods lack explicit local control: geometric adherence is often defined by a global control strength, and appearance cannot be specified locally.
